sections.h2: Selling an Oak Creek house quickly
sections.html:
Fast sales in this city tend to follow one of two patterns: a buyer paying cash and accepting the house untouched, or a listing that is priced right and ready from day one. The city is a lakeshore suburb just south of Milwaukee with a blend of owners and renters, so you may meet families and investors alike. On either path the transfer fee, the condition report and the deed filing all remain.

Get these items together before you call anyone, and offers will be simple to compare.

  • Your latest tax bill, which carries the ten-digit parcel number
  • A payoff figure from your lender
  • Permit paperwork for any work since you bought the house
  • A written inventory of fixtures and appliances that stay or go
  • A first draft of your Real Estate Condition Report answers

Put three questions to each buyer or agent. When is closing? Which fees come out of my proceeds? What if the inspection finds a problem?

Population has reached 38,296, a 4.9 percent rise over the 2020 base. Among 15,728 households, 57.5 percent are owners and the rest rent. Typical figures: $331,700 for an owner-occupied home, $1,922 monthly owner cost with a mortgage ($838 without), $1,452 for gross rent and $96,555 for household income.

Newer housing sets the bar your listing is measured against. Drexel Town Square, an 85-acre site on part of the old AC Spark Plug grounds, combines shops, restaurants, housing, a hotel and the civic center, and a Millwood Glen development by Veridian Homes adds more. Price with those options in mind.

Commuters look at access. The city has direct entry to I-94 and sits near Milwaukee's airport, and its position on the southwestern shore of Lake Michigan, with Milwaukee, Greenfield, South Milwaukee, Caledonia, Franklin and Greendale as neighbors, is worth naming in a listing.

One district, Oak Creek-Franklin Joint, covers the whole city plus a seven-square-mile part of Franklin. Its seven elementary schools are Carollton, Cedar Hills, Deerfield, Edgewood, Forest Ridge, Meadowview and Shepard Hills.

Plumbing, electrical, heating and air conditioning installs, new construction and alterations all run through Inspection Services. To book an inspection, call 414-766-7002 and have your permit number and a contact name ready. Time slots come in two blocks: morning, 9 a.m. to noon, and afternoon, noon to 3 p.m. Same-day requests are refused. You can follow status on BS&A Online by searching your address.

A permit an earlier owner skipped can be flagged by a buyer's inspector. Phone Inspection Services at 414-766-7002 to learn what is on file, then decide between closing out the permit and disclosing the gap.

Taxes can be paid four ways. Pay online through the Milwaukee County portal with the ten-digit parcel number from your bill. Or mail a payment, walk it into City Hall, or visit a partner bank branch, an option that runs through January 31. Online, cards cost 2.55 percent with a $2 minimum, and an e-check costs $1.50. Between February 1 and July 31, mail payments to the Treasurer, City of Oak Creek, 8040 S 6th Street.

City Hall takes payments in person from 8 am to 4 pm, Monday through Friday, with limited check-only service in December and January. Your closing agent can explain proration of the current bill. Separately, the treasurer's office can issue a statement of what your parcel owes, special charges included, which keeps the closing figure in line with city records.

Wis. Stat. 709.02 asks sellers of one-to-four unit homes to deliver a finished Real Estate Condition Report inside 10 days after contract acceptance. A late report lets the buyer rescind during the next two business days and take deposits back. Under Wis. Stat. 709.01, court-appointed fiduciaries who never lived in the property are excused, and so are transfers exempt from the fee.

Take foreclosure as a test case. Wis. Stat. 77.25(14) exempts a foreclosure transfer or deed in lieu to a mortgage holder. A voluntary seller who sells ahead of foreclosure gets no such break and must still give the report.

Oak Creek lies in Milwaukee County, so your deed goes to the Register of Deeds at 901 N. 9th Street, Room 103. You owe the state transfer fee of 30 cents per $100 of value under Wis. Stat. 77.22, and the register collects it. Add a $30 recording charge.

Milwaukee County recording at a glance
Recording stepWhat to expect

Contact414-278-4005 or RODrecordings@milwaukeecountywi.gov

Whether a sale can go forward quickly turns on how title was held. After a spouse dies, the county accepts the Termination of Decedent's Interest form (HT-110), priced at $30, and Wis. Stat. 77.25(11) supplies an exemption. A personal representative selling an estate home should confirm authority with the probate court or an attorney first. A buyer's title company will ask who may sign.

The order is simple once you know it. After the contract is signed, you finish the condition report within 10 days. Request the tax statement from the treasurer, and ask your closing agent how the bill will be prorated. Have the deed prepared, file the electronic transfer return and take the receipt, the original deed and payment to the county office. If an inspection report names open permits, call Inspection Services early, because inspections cannot be booked for the same day.

A cash sale reduces the work of showings and buyer financing. It does not remove the report, the return or the recording. Whichever buyer you choose, compare offers by the net left after your mortgage payoff, tax proration, city charges and closing costs, and keep the written offer with your records.

faqs.q: Does Milwaukee County accept a card for recording a deed?
faqs.a: No. The office takes cash, checks or money orders payable to the Register of Deeds. The $30 fee applies per document, and any transfer fee on your electronic return receipt is paid at the same time.

faqs.q: Can I sell an Oak Creek house after an owner has died?
faqs.a: Often yes, though the paperwork depends on how title was held. After a spouse's death the county uses form HT-110 for $30. A personal representative should confirm authority with the probate court or an attorney first, because the deed needs a signature from someone with legal authority to sign.

faqs.q: How soon can I get an inspection in Oak Creek?
faqs.a: Call 414-766-7002 with your permit number and a contact name. Same-day inspections are not offered, and requests are filled in morning or afternoon blocks in the order received, so book early if a closing date is close.

faqs.q: Do I need a condition report for a foreclosure sale?
faqs.a: A transfer exempt from the fee is also excused from the report under Wis. Stat. 709.01, and a foreclosure or deed in lieu to a mortgage holder is one of those. An owner selling voluntarily before foreclosure must still provide it.

faqs.q: Who can tell me what I owe in property tax?
faqs.a: The City Treasurer at City Hall takes payments and can confirm your parcel's balance. In-person hours are 8 am to 4 pm, Monday through Friday, with limited check-only service in December and January.
